newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil chief sees sharp fall in profits.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil chief sees sharp fall in profits.

text.p: Japanese oil firms' combined profits for the last business year which ended on March 31 are expected to fall sharply from a year earlier, the nation's oil industry body said on Wednesday.
"Current profits of Japan's oil firms put together, are expected to fall by almost 30 percent from a year earlier," Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ) chairman Yuji Idemitsu told a news conference.
Idemitsu said the estimate included firms which have already announced their earnings for January to December 1996, and those which follow an April-March business year.
Idemitsu said the fall stemmed from not being able to immediately pass on the rising cost of procuring crude to the wholesale price and a weak domestic oil product retail market.
A time lag occurs in passing on costs to the wholesale price because Japanese oil firms use crude prices during the previous month to decide the wholesale price for the next month.
Although the outlook for the industry as a whole was bleak, Idemitsu said earnings were expected to differ greatly depending on the company.
"Some companies are expected to see very sharp downturns in profits while others' only a small dip," Idemitsu said.
For the year ending December 1996, Mobil Sekiyu KK reported its current profits fell by 10.2 percent compared to a year earlier, while Showa Shell Sekiyu KK current profits were down 36.2 percent.
